Goodfellow Prospect, subsalt foram report, 23500 to 24700 = salt inclusion analysis, foram species abundance and diversity chart available, see report for details - the upper one-fourth of the drilled subsalt interval is Late Oligocene in age (with fairly minor rubble zone, probably limited to the first subsalt sample at 24800’-24830’ accompanied by rare Miocene planktics) - this interval is typified by the sporadic occurrences of Paragloborotalia opima s.s. (early Late Oligocene [P21b]) with other Late Oligocene representatives - possible slight age progression into the late Early Oligocene is detected at 26540’-26570’ [P19] or at 26660’-26690’ [P21a] - underlying this Upper Oligocene part is an interval of conspicuous pink/brown limestone microlithology downhole, first marked by the Late Eocene species of Turborotalia at 26720’-26750’ then by mixed Late Cretaceous (Campanian-Maastrichtian) and Middle Eocene planktic forams at 26750’-26780’ - a reliable within-Maastrichtian planktic foram assemblage is found at 26990’-27020’ - the base of this limestone unit represents the entries of several planktic species of the middle Early Paleocene - thus this limestone section is likely an overturned block, from the middle to lower part of the drilled interval is a highly expanded section of the Wilcox Formation with generally very low-abundance of forams in which two discernible biostratigraphic events occur, - one is the increase in agglutinated benthic Bathysiphon spp at 28130’-28160’ containing large  thick-walled morphology (Bathysiphon eocenicus) as a common element - this event is usually known to develop at the top of Wilcox 3 (middle Late Paleocene) - another is a pulse of the planktic assemblage from near the Paleocene/Eocene boundary [P6B] at 32120’-32150’ - these observations also imply an age reversal through this thick Wilcox section.
